excerpt: Prelint reviews every pull request for the product decisions it makes, checks them against your docs and past decisions, and keeps a decision ledger. $1 per review.
content:
Prelint reviews pull requests for product decisions rather than code quality. Coding agents can write code that passes review and CI but quietly changes how the product behaves: skipping a notification, changing invoice terms, adding a dependency nobody approved or inventing a requirement. Prelint posts a short "decision review" on each pull request listing the decisions the change makes and checks them against your architecture decision records (ADRs), docs, specs and earlier decisions. You agree, agree with concerns or disagree.

Every review is added to a decision ledger that records who made each decision, when, where it came from and whether a person or an AI made it. Your coding agents can search that ledger through a CLI or MCP before writing code. Prelint charges $1 per completed review with no seats or subscription, and open-source projects are free.

Prelint was founded by Wojtek Szkutnik, with co-founders Irka Pawlowski (CMO) and Krzysztof Kulig (CTO), according to their Product Hunt profiles. It launched there on 29 July 2026 and finished #1 for the day and the week, with 579 upvotes and 134 comments. It has 3 reviews on Product Hunt averaging 5 out of 5 (as of 14 October 2026).

We have not tested Prelint ourselves. This page brings together its official site and pricing page, its Product Hunt launch and the public pricing pages of comparable tools, and says where each fact comes from.

profile.platform: GitHub pull-request reviews, CLI and MCP
profile.summary_short: Reviews each pull request for the product decisions it makes and keeps a decision ledger

gallery.alt: Prelint graphic 'AI code reviewers check if your code is technically correct. Prelint checks if it does the right thing' with a bot comment listing four product decisions in a billing change
Prelint chart of findings by type, such as stale references, vendor conflicts, spec deviations and data safety
Prelint CLI searching the decision ledger for 'pricing', returning recorded statements with their IDs

paragraphs: Wojtek Szkutnik says coding agents now produce more code than most teams can properly review, and the bigger risk is not bad code but good code that quietly builds the wrong product.

He saw this on large production projects: a change would pass technical review and CI but skip an agreed architecture pattern, add an unapproved dependency, change a permission rule or invent a business requirement. Nobody had made that decision, yet it was now part of the product. Prelint is built to catch those decisions before they ship.
launch_story.attribution: Wojtek Szkutnik, founder, on Product Hunt

use_cases: Catching AI-written changes that contradict your ADRs, specs or billing policy
Keeping a searchable record of who decided what, and whether an AI or a person made the call
Giving coding agents your past decisions as context before they write code
Reviewing decisions on a solo project shipped daily with Claude Code

fit: ship a lot of AI-written pull requests and can't review every product decision by hand
keep ADRs, specs or policy docs you want code checked against
prefer paying per review over per-seat subscriptions
not_fit: want line-by-line code-quality feedback: Prelint describes its job as checking whether code does the right thing, while other AI reviewers check whether it is technically correct
don't work with pull requests at all

pricing.intro: Prelint charges per completed review from a prepaid balance. No seats, subscriptions or minimums. Prices are in US dollars.

plans.name: Pay per review
plans.detail: Spec checks, decision compliance, inline findings and a summary comment on one pull request; $10 free credit at sign-up with no card

plans.name: Open source
plans.detail: Open-source projects are free, according to the pricing page

notes: Credits never expire. Top up any amount from $10 to $1,000; auto-recharge is on by default ($20 when the balance falls below $10) and can be changed or switched off.
Failed, cancelled and timed-out reviews are free, and CI bots never trigger reviews. Re-reviews after new commits cost $1 each.
Prelint says most teams spend $40 to $80 a month. You can set a monthly spending cap.

alternatives.intro: AI pull-request reviewers. They focus mainly on code correctness, which Prelint positions itself alongside. Prices are from each company's own pricing page on 14 October 2026.

items.name: CodeRabbit
items.what: AI code reviews in pull requests, the CLI, IDEs and agent loops
items.difference: Per-seat pricing and a focus on code quality; Prelint checks product decisions against your docs and charges per review.

items.name: Greptile
items.what: AI code reviewer that understands your whole codebase
items.difference: Reviews code with full-repository context and custom rules; it doesn't keep a ledger of product decisions.

liked: The 'decision ledger, not a code reviewer' idea
Catching your own documented decisions going stale against your code
asked: Whether it helps a one-person company with no Slack, meetings or tickets (yes if you work with pull requests, the founder said)
Whether promises made by support staff can count as decisions (the founder suggested support tools query Prelint's MCP instead)

quotes.text: The "decision ledger, not a code reviewer" framing is the part I'd have paid for a year ago.
quotes.author: Rick Wise

quotes.text: I had wrongly assumed drift was a coordination problem
quotes.author: Chris Mongeon

pros: No seats or subscription: $1 per completed review
Free for open-source projects; credits never expire
Builds a searchable decision record that agents can query
Failed or cancelled reviews aren't charged
cons: Cost grows with the number of pull requests and re-reviews
Most useful when you have docs, ADRs or specs to check against
Not a replacement for code-quality review

quotes.author: Rick Wise
quotes.text: Asked how Prelint helps a one-person company without Slack, meetings or tickets to learn from.
quotes.reply: Wojtek Szkutnik said that if you work with pull requests you would still get a lot of value without those artefacts.

x.none: Apart from Prelint's own account, we found no posts on X clearly about the product.

faq.a: A pull-request reviewer that lists the product decisions a change makes, checks them against your ADRs, docs and earlier decisions, and records them in a decision ledger.
$1 per completed review from prepaid credits, with $10 free at sign-up and no card. Open-source projects are free. Prelint says most teams spend $40 to $80 a month.
Not in the usual sense. It checks whether code does the right thing for the product, alongside tools that check whether it is technically correct.

faq.q: Is it useful for solo developers?
faq.a: The founder says yes if you work with pull requests, even without Slack, meetings or tickets.
Yes. You can set a monthly limit; reviews pause when it is reached.
